games.2026_02_DET_BUF: Buffalo enters as the third-highest-rated team after its win in Houston, and Detroit's rating slipped after needing overtime to beat New Orleans at home. The Lions' problem on a short week is the offensive line: left guard Christian Mahogany is doubtful, rookie right tackle Blake Miller and center Juice Scruggs are questionable, and Cade Mays is already on IR. Buffalo's James Cook is questionable with a hamstring. It is the first regular-season game at the new Highmark Stadium, and model and market agree on Bills by about four and a half.
games.2026_02_CAR_ATL: Two depleted rosters and a coin flip. Atlanta lost Da'Shawn Hand for the season in Week 1 and still has Jalon Walker on IR and James Pearce Jr. suspended, Drake London is questionable with a shoulder, and Cooper Rush is the likely starter again unless Penix or Tua is cleared. Carolina is worse off on the line: both starting tackles are out at least through Week 4, Nic Scourton is done for the year, and the defense just allowed 59 points. The model has the Falcons by three at home on the strength of the quarterback gap being smaller than it looks; the market has Carolina by 1.5, and the blend lands on Atlanta by less than a point.
games.2026_02_CIN_HOU: Houston rated well above Cincinnati entering the season, but the injuries are one-sided. The Texans have Braden Smith and Jayden Higgins on IR and lost two more linebackers, Henry To'oTo'o and Jake Hummel, in Week 1 with E.J. Speed already out. Cincinnati is the healthiest team on the slate and gets the full Joe Burrow adjustment, the largest quarterback boost in the model, after a 1-8 record without him last year. The roof will be closed. Model and market both make Houston a three-point favorite.
games.2026_02_CLE_TB: Tampa Bay rated five and a half points better than Cleveland before the season and the gap widened after the Browns' 34-10 loss in Jacksonville. Todd Monken kept Deshaun Watson as the starter despite a poor debut. Both teams are relatively healthy for this one, so the number is about ratings and weather: 89 degrees with a 70 percent thunderstorm chance compresses the margin slightly. The model has the Bucs by six, the market by 8.5, and the blend by about seven.
games.2026_02_GB_NYJ: Green Bay's rating fell more than a point after the loss in Minnesota and the Packers are still without Micah Parsons and Josh Jacobs, with two starting linemen questionable. But the Jets are worse off: their rating is the lowest on the slate, Minkah Fitzpatrick and first-round receiver Omar Cooper Jr. both went down early in Week 1 and are doubtful, and Joseph Ossai is out. The model makes Green Bay a six-point road favorite, more than the market's 4.5.
games.2026_02_MIN_CHI: The biggest model-versus-market gap of the week. Chicago's rating rose after the 59-point outburst in Carolina, but the Bears have Ozzy Trapilo and Tyrique Stevenson questionable and three defenders on PUP, a 2.5-point injury hit. Minnesota turns to Carson Wentz with Kyler Murray in concussion protocol; Wentz still grades a bit above what the Vikings fielded in 2025, so the model does not treat the swap as a collapse. The data alone has this a pick; the market has Chicago by 5.5, and the blend settles on Bears by three.
games.2026_02_NO_BAL: Baltimore's 41-23 win in Indianapolis was the best opponent-adjusted performance of Week 1 and lifted the Ravens to fourth in the ratings. New Orleans is missing Cameron Jordan, has Alvin Kamara questionable at best, and lost rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson to IR. Zay Flowers is questionable for Baltimore with a hamstring. Model and market agree on Ravens by eight and a half to nine.
games.2026_02_PHI_TEN: Philadelphia's rating fell after the narrow win over Washington and the Eagles lost Landon Dickerson to IR, with Jonathan Greenard still questionable. Tennessee's rating dropped too after the loss to the Jets. The model has the Eagles by under five on the road, the market by seven; the blend is six, which keeps Philadelphia a Moderate pick rather than a High one.
games.2026_02_PIT_NE: New England's rating takes the biggest injury hit on the slate: A.J. Brown went on IR with a high-ankle sprain, Harold Landry is on PUP, and TreVeyon Henderson is only trending toward his debut. Pittsburgh came out of Week 1 healthy apart from DeShon Elliott on IR. The model still likes the Patriots at home by nearly four, but the market's 5.5 looks generous, and the blend is 4.7.
games.2026_02_JAX_DEN: The one game where the data and the market pick different teams. Jacksonville's rout of Cleveland made it the second-highest-rated team in the league, and Denver's 31-10 loss in Kansas City, with Jonathon Cooper still on the exempt list, dropped the Broncos below average. On the data alone the Jaguars are five-and-a-half-point road favorites; the market has Denver by 2.5. The blend gives Jacksonville the narrowest of edges, so this is a coin flip either way.
games.2026_02_LV_LAC: The Chargers rated as a slight favorite before the season, but the offensive line is without Tyler Biadasz, Denzel Perryman is on IR, and Ladd McConkey and Elijah Molden are questionable after the loss to Arizona. Las Vegas gets the Kirk Cousins upgrade over last year's quarterback play and has Brock Bowers questionable to return from a meniscus trim. The model has Los Angeles by two and a half; the market says seven, and the blend is about five.
games.2026_02_MIA_SF: The largest gap on the slate. San Francisco came out of Melbourne healthy, with Kittle, Bosa and McCaffrey all playing, and its rating rose three points on the 27-7 win. Miami is a bottom-three team by rating with a first-year starter at quarterback and Kenneth Grant on IR. The model has the 49ers by twelve, the market by 13.5, and the simulation gives Miami roughly one chance in six.
games.2026_02_SEA_ARI: Seattle is the top-rated team in the model but plays without Sam Darnold, who strained a hip on the first series against New England and is expected to miss the game. Drew Lock costs the Seahawks about two and a half points, and Nick Emmanwori remains questionable. Arizona is short James Conner and has two starters questionable, but its rating jumped after the upset in Los Angeles. Roof closed. The model has Seattle by five and a half, the market by 4.5.
games.2026_02_WAS_DAL: Two below-average teams getting worse. Dallas lost Tyler Smith to IR and will be without Malik Hooker and DeMarvion Overshown; Washington is still without Laremy Tunsil, Johnny Newton and Trey Amos, and Frankie Luvu and Chig Okonkwo are questionable after Week 1 exits. Jayden Daniels grades as a modest upgrade on last year's Commanders quarterback play. Roof closed, model and market both around Cowboys by three.
games.2026_02_IND_KC: Kansas City's rating climbed after the Monday-night win and Mahomes came through his return healthy, but Josh Simmons and Chamarri Conner remain questionable. Indianapolis dropped more than three points after being routed at home by Baltimore. The weather is the wild card: a 70 percent rain chance and 15 mph wind at Arrowhead pull the margin and the total down. The model has the Chiefs by five and a half, the market by 6.5.
games.2026_02_NYG_LA: The Rams fell three points in the ratings after the loss in Melbourne and then lost Myles Garrett to IR until at least Week 6, with Aaron Donald still questionable to make his debut. New York's Jaxson Dart played well in Dallas and Malik Nabers is back. Los Angeles gets extra rest after its Thursday game in Australia. The model has the Rams by five, the market by seven, and the blend by six.
